title: The Cosmic Opening and the First Draft
paragraphs: §The Life-Light
Before anything existed—before the universe, before time itself—the Word was already there. The Word was face to face with God, and the Word was God. He was with God, ready and present, from day one.

Everything was created through him. Not a single thing—nothing!—came into being without him. What came into existence was Life itself, and that Life was Light for everyone to live by. The Life-Light blazed out into the darkness, and the darkness couldn't put it out.

There was a man named John, sent by God to point everyone toward the Life-Light. His job was to show people where to look and who to believe in. John wasn't the Light himself—he was just there to point the way to the Light.

The Life-Light was the real deal: everyone who steps into Life, he brings into Light. He was right here in the world—the world that was made through him—and yet the world didn't even notice him. He came to his own people, but they didn't want him. But everyone who did want him, everyone who believed he was who he claimed to be and trusted he would do what he said—he gave them their true selves, their child-of-God selves. These are God-born people, not born by blood or human desire or anyone's decision.

Then the ultimate plot twist: The Word became flesh and blood and moved into our neighborhood. We saw his glory with our own eyes—the one-of-a-kind glory, like Father, like Son—generous inside and out, true from start to finish.
John pointed him out and shouted, "This is the One! The One I told you was coming after me but is actually ahead of me. He has always been ahead of me—he always gets the first word."

We all live off his endless generosity—gift after gift after gift. We got the basics from Moses, and then this overflowing giving and receiving, this endless knowing and understanding of God—all of it came through Jesus, the Messiah. No one has ever seen God, not even a glimpse. But this one-of-a-kind God-Expression, who lives at the very heart of the Father, has made him as plain as day.
§Thunder in the Desert

When the religious leaders in Jerusalem sent a group of priests and officials to ask John who he was, he didn't dodge. He was completely straight with them. He told the plain truth: "I am not the Messiah."
They pressed him: "Then who are you? Elijah?" "I'm not." "The Prophet?" "No."
Frustrated, they said, "Then who ARE you?! We need an answer to take back to the people who sent us. Tell us something—anything—about yourself!"
"I'm thunder in the desert: 'Make the road straight for God!' I'm doing exactly what the prophet Isaiah said would happen."
The interrogation squad was from the Pharisee party, and they had their own question: "If you're not the Messiah, not Elijah, and not the Prophet—then why are you baptizing people?!"

John answered, "I only baptize with water. But right here among you is standing someone you don't even recognize. He comes after me, but he's not second place to me—I'm not even worthy to hold his coat for him."
(All of these conversations happened in Bethany on the other side of the Jordan River, where John was baptizing at the time.)
§The God-Revealer

The very next day, John saw Jesus coming toward him and yelled out, "Here he is—God's Passover Lamb! He takes away the sin of the world! This is the man I've been telling you about: 'the One who comes after me but is really ahead of me.' I didn't know who he was at first—I only knew my job: to get Israel ready to recognize him as the God-Revealer. That's why I came baptizing with water, giving you a good bath, scrubbing the sins from your life so you can get a fresh start with God."

John backed up his testimony with this: "I watched the Spirit come down out of the sky like a dove and make himself at home in him. I keep telling you, I knew nothing about him except this: The One who sent me to baptize with water told me, 'The One you see the Spirit come down and stay on—that's the One who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.' That's exactly what I saw happen, and I'm telling you straight: there is zero doubt about it. THIS is the Son of God."
§Come, See for Yourself
The next day John was back at his post with two of his disciples watching. He looked up, saw Jesus walking nearby, and said, "Here he is—God's Passover Lamb."
The two disciples heard him and went after Jesus. Jesus looked over his shoulder and said to them, "What are you after?" They said, "Rabbi" (which means "Teacher"), "where are you staying?"
He replied, "Come along and see for yourself." They came, saw where he was staying, and ended up hanging out with him for the rest of the day. It was late afternoon when this happened.

Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, was one of the two who heard John's testimony and followed Jesus. The first thing he did after finding where Jesus lived was track down his own brother Simon, telling him, "We've found the Messiah!" (that is, "Christ"). He brought him straight to Jesus. Jesus took one look at him and said, "You're Simon, John's son? From now on your name is Cephas" (or Peter, which means "Rock").
The next day Jesus decided to head for Galilee. When he got there, he ran into Philip and said, "Come, follow me." (Philip's hometown was Bethsaida—same town as Andrew and Peter.)

Philip went and found Nathanael and told him, "We've found the One Moses wrote about in the Law, the One the prophets preached about. It's Jesus, Joseph's son, the one from Nazareth!" Nathanael said, "Nazareth? You've got to be kidding." But Philip said, "Come and see for yourself."
When Jesus saw him coming he said, "There's a real Israelite—not a single fake bone in his body."
Nathanael said, "Where did you get that idea? You don't even know me." Jesus answered, "One day, long before Philip called you over here, I saw you under the fig tree."
Nathanael exclaimed, "Rabbi! You are the Son of God, the King of Israel!"

Jesus said, "You became a believer just because I said I saw you sitting under the fig tree one day? You haven't seen anything yet! Before this is over, you're going to see heaven ripped open and God's angels going up and down on the Son of Man."
